chapter: Picnics, wagon advertising and saloon work
title: Bucking contests between wagon bands
summary: Rival wagon bands played against each other with applause deciding, and uptown favored Jack Carey while downtown favored Olympia.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: When you went out to advertise, did you sometimes meet other bands on wagons?
Oh, sure. Sure, we used to buck, we'd call that bucking. We'd say we'd stop this corner, and the fellow would say, Well, there's a kid right there at the next corner.
You'd run?
Well, we'd make a round. Say, let's go get him. They'd come around, a couple of blouse come around, and backbomb, you know. And we'd hit about our best, and it hit their best. And pull off.
Did you both play at the same time, or one and then? No, no, uh-uh.
One band would play. One at a time?
Yeah. And then the other one? That's right.
You wouldn't play at the same time?
No, no, oh no. Did they tie the wheels together sometimes? Of the two wagons? No.
Oh, no.

Sometimes people told us they'd tie the two wagons together so the other band couldn't get away. Couldn't get away. Oh, well. You don't remember that. Matt Carey told me that. What? Matt Carey told me that. He said sometimes they would tie the wagons, and everybody was scared of Kepard, he said. So whatever Kepard's band would, anybody that Kepard would play with would come, they would tie it so that the other band could make a getaway, you know?
That was Freddie Kepard. Yeah. That was Olympia. Olympia band. Mm-hmm.
Well when one band played against the other, then how would you tell who won that contest?
Well, it was left to the majority of people, you know. Was it by applause?
Yeah. Exciting?
That's it, excitement and applause. That's right.
Would the people say anything to you? Huh? Would the people say anything at the end of a number?
Well.
They would come up and tell you?
I'd say, well, they had some people in different parts of the town had their preference.
You mean sometimes we're poor? All bands. More popular in certain sections.

That's right. That's right. Now Uptown, Jack Carrey had it Uptown. Everybody's for Jack. You come downtown, well everybody's for Olympia, the Imperial, or Superior. That's downtown. You usually played with Jack Carrey then.
Did you play many wagon jobs with other bands sometimes? Oh yes. Just anyone that would happen to play?
